title: A functor is a left adjoint exactly when the hom-functors hom_B(F a, b) are representable
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.5.10 at source lines 1010-1016: a functor F : A -> B is a left adjoint exactly when for every b : B the functor a |-> hom_B(Fa,b) is representable. The 46-line proof builds a quasi-inverse in both directions and then checks two round trips that live in different types, so neither can be waved through. The direction from representability must invent the functor action G(g) := gamma_{Gb,b'}(g o eps_b) together with eta_a := gamma_{a,Fa}(1_{Fa}) and eps_b := inverse gamma_{Gb,b}(1_{Gb}) (lines 1022-1025); the reverse direction must produce the whole family gamma from G and eta with inverse built from F and eps, using the triangle identities (lines 1028-1039). The first round trip is a rewrite of G(f) o eta_a that consumes naturality of gamma (lines 1041-1049), and the second recovers the hom-action of G from G(g o eps_b) o eta_{Gb} = G(g) and then re-derives eta and eps from their defining clauses (lines 1051-1061). The statement records neither the naturality equation that gamma has to satisfy nor the two composites.
